summary: [standards] The failure halves of crate-1-2 F2 and F4 are the crate's functions driven with canon's table as a fixture, not something canon does: atip.crate12.15 (rows with another exit/retryable, STOPPED_MIDWAY at exit 2 for 1.2) calls atip::registration_problem on synthetic values, and atip.crate12.17 (reason of a missing code, wrong length, duplicate probe row) calls atip::reason_of_code, reasons_with_exit and with_row under catch_unwind. They would pass whatever canon registers for those paths and only fail if the pinned crate regresses (mutation probe: dropping the retryable check or the sort in the atip copy fails them). Canon-side faults are caught by the other halves (probes: changing PLAN_STALE retryable fails 14 and 15; an unsorted reasons list fails 16). Honest as a pin of the crate version, thin as canon behaviour; the brief's F2/F4 failure paths have no other canon-observable form, since canon registers no STOPPED_MIDWAY row. Accepted, signed. Blast radius: a canon table row that the crate would reject at compile time (a reason of an absent code) stops the build, which no runtime test exercises.
